description: CT-RATE is a public dataset comprising 50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices) from 25,692 non-contrast chest CT scans of 21,304 unique patients, each paired with a corresponding radiology text report. Each volume is also annotated with 18 abnormality labels extracted from the reports using an automated text classifier. The dataset is designed to support development of foundation models for 3D medical imaging, including contrastive language-image pretraining and vision-language AI assistants.
name: CT-RATE
publisher: Istanbul Medipol University / University of Zurich
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each CT volume is accompanied by one radiology report (authored by a radiologist) and 18 binary abnormality labels extracted automatically from that report.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m text encoder's performance was evaluated on a 200-report validation set. Precision, recall, and F1 scores were computed per abnormality. Results showed robust classification across all 18 abnormalities, with most achieving F1 scores of 0.95–1.00 (e.g., Pericardial effusion F1=1.00, Pleural effusion F1=1.00, Peribronchial thickening F1=1.00, Interlobular septal thickening F1=1.00; lowest was Bronchiectasis at F1=0.95).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels for 18 distinct abnormalities were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. To develop this classifier, 1,000 reports were manually annotated by merging findings and impression sections, creating a multi-label dataset. Conditions not referenced in either section were considered absent. Similar conditions were grouped (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; various lung opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules). The annotated reports were split 80/20 into training (800) and validation (200) sets. A pretrained language model (RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m) was finetuned on this dataset and then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset originates from a single institution (Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital) in a single geographic and clinical setting (Türkiye), which may limit generalizability to other populations. The authors acknowledge that biases inherent to this single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training. An ablation study showed performance increases with larger training sets, suggesting that incorporating data from multiple institutions and more diverse patient populations could further enhance model robustness. CT-CLIP also depends on the specific terminology used in reports and the choice of prompts during zero-shot detection; variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy.
rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE was curated from chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. In clinical practice, CT volumes are reconstructed with various techniques for specific diagnostic requirements; every reconstructed volume from the hospital database was incorporated. The cohort was divided into 20,000 patients for training and 1,304 for validation. Patients range in age from 18 to 102 years (mean 48.8, mode 40). Sex distribution is 41.6% female and 58.4% male. Scanners used: 61.5% Philips, 30.1% Siemens, 8.4% PNMS.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes acquired at Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, along with structured radiology reports authored by radiologists. Reports contain four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression. CT volumes are provided in various resolutions (65.4% in 512×512 px, 4.2% in 768×768 px, 30.4% in 1024×1024 px). Pixel spacing in the axial plane ranges from 0.227 to 1.416 mm (mean 0.605 mm); slice thickness ranges from 0.035 to 6 mm (mean 1.231 mm); number of slices per volume ranges from 100 to 600 (mean 304.7). Original reports were in Turkish.
rai:dataLimitations: First, the dataset is from a single institution and geographic setting, limiting generalizability. Second, CT-CLIP depends on specific terminology in reports and prompt choice during zero-shot detection. Third, the current models are limited to chest CT volumes and do not cover other 3D imaging modalities (MRI, PET) or other anatomical regions. Fourth, the quality of CT-CHAT-generated reports remains insufficient for clinical use. Fifth, detailed metadata for the second external validation set (UPMC) is not publicly available as it is a private dataset.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: CT volumes were reconstructed using various techniques to suit different window settings (e.g., sharper kernels for lung abnormalities, smoother kernels for mediastinal assessment). Every reconstructed volume from the hospital database was incorporated, resulting in 50,188 reconstructed volumes from 25,692 scans. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using TotalSegmentator and are included in the dataset. A VQA dataset of over 2.7 million question-answer pairs was derived from CT-RATE reports using Llama 3.1 8B for CT-CHAT training.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each CT volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. Volumes were then center-cropped or padded to a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. CT volumes were converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from metadata. HU values were clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, values were normalized to a range of -1 to 1. Each volume's orientation was standardized by examining its metadata. Volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Radiology reports were anonymized (personal information removed via regular expressions), translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and reviewed/corrected by bilingual final-year medical students.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as future work. As an initial step, organ-level anatomical segmentation labels generated using TotalSegmentator are openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CT-RATE addresses the scarcity of comprehensive 3D medical imaging datasets paired with textual reports, enabling development of AI foundation models for 3D medical imaging. The open-source release aims to reduce the workload on radiologists, potentially improve diagnostic accuracy, and support patient care in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The dataset and associated models lay groundwork for future innovations in medical AI. The authors note that substantial progress is still needed before clinical deployment, and challenges such as robustness, interpretability, regulatory compliance, and prospective validation must be addressed.
rai:dataUseCases: Training contrastive language-image pretraining models for 3D chest CT (CT-CLIP); multi-abnormality detection in chest CT volumes; CT volume-to-volume retrieval; report-to-volume retrieval; training vision-language AI assistants for 3D chest CT (CT-CHAT); visual question answering on chest CT; radiology report generation; supervised classification baseline training; anatomical segmentation (organ-level labels included); future multi-abnormality segmentation and localization research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned for automated multi-abnormality label extraction from radiology reports); Google Translate API (for translating reports from Turkish to English); Llama 3.1 8B (for generating VQA question-answer pairs for CT-CHAT training); TotalSegmentator (for generating organ-level anatomical segmentation labels); a state-of-the-art 3D nodule segmentation algorithm (for extracting nodule metadata including lobar location, centroid, diameters, and volumes).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: All chest CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports were anonymized before release. Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. CT volume metadata was also de-identified (all identifying information about patients and medical professionals removed). Ethical approval was granted by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee at Istanbul Medipol University (E-10840098-772.02-6841, 27/10/2023).

null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned; annotation was done by bilingual medical students and automated tools without specifying a platform.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper only mentions that bilingual final-year medical students reviewed report translations; no further demographic details about annotators are provided.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling in the CT-RATE collection process; volumes with contrast material or non-chest body parts were excluded but this is a quality filter, not missing data imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described for missing values in the dataset itself; padding of CT volumes to consistent resolution is covered under preprocessing.
